images.filename: Trees and Grave Markers on the Slope at Andrew Johnson National Cemetery (39d25a0c-38dd-4cd6-9933-ddc0d9d25504).jpg
images.caption:
Uniform white marble grave markers stand in rows along the side of a slope, with a scattering of tall evergreen trees.
The cemetery is situated on a steep knoll known as Monument Hill. Historically the scenic qualities and panoramic view of the area and the somewhat isolated location of the cemetery reflected associations with the rural cemetery movement that was a prominent design ideal for burial places during Johnson’s lifetime.
Keywords: cemetery; national cemetery; grave marker

images.caption:
Scattered, mature trees shade rows of marble grave markers in an area of turf, sloping toward a hill in the distance.
In 1875, Andrew Johnson was buried atop what was then called Signal Hill. In 1906, a national cemetery was established on the site.
Keywords: national cemetery; cemetery; cultural landscape; grave marker

images.filename: Flag and Grave Markers on Monument Hill (8e889bf8-ecb9-473b-8517-377cf2058440).jpg
images.caption:
Mature trees shade rows of marble grave markers on a steep slope, with a flagpole at the top in the distance.
The cemetery flagstaff, located at the center of the memorial approach on the north slope of 
Monument Hill, was erected in 1908. The 75-foot cast-iron flagstaff was recycled from the mast of a retired navy vessel from “stock on hand at the St. Louis Depot.”
Keywords: national cemetery; cemetery; cultural landscape; grave marker; flag

images.caption:
A pathway with wide steps and a metal railing leads up the side of a grassy slope, surrounded by rows of marble grave markers and mature evergreen trees.
During the Mission 66 period of NPS development, walkways were added to the slopes of Monument Hill improve circulation through the cemetery.
Keywords: national cemetery; cemetery; walkway; cultural landscape
